sentences.text:
For the State : Mr. Tarun Kumar, A.P.P.
 ----
 06/Dated: 03rd October, 2024 1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned counsel for the State.

2. The applicant-husband, who is in custody since 25.11.2022, has approached this Court for grant of regular bail in connection with S.T No.107 of 2023, arising out of Bistupur P.S. Case No.92 of 2022,
corresponding to G.R No.2022 of 2022, registered for the offence under Section 498A & 306 of the Indian Penal Code, pending in the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-V-cum-FTC (CAW),
at Jamshedpur.

3. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant(s) that complete set of FIR along with its enclosure have been annexed with this bail application and there is no suppression on his/her part.
4. Innocence has been claimed by the learned counsel for the applicant and undertaking has been given for participation in the trial.
It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that out of four charge sheeted witnesses, two have already been examined.

On the above basis,
prayer for bail has been made.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for bail.
6. Considering the nature of allegation and the material available on record, I am not inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the prayer for bail of the applicant is hereby, rejected.
7. However, learned Trial Court is directed to expedite the trial and conclude the same within six months.
